topics.title: Market overview
topics.summary: Read broad participation, leadership, movers, and market context together.

sections.heading: What the overview shows
paragraphs: The overview brings together benchmark context, advancing and declining participation, breadth history, leading securities, daily movers, and the selected market-health model. Market Reading cards report their underlying observations independently of the composite health score; a missing or withheld score does not erase those facts. Daily movers compare with the prior close and show the corresponding industry when available. A benchmark gain alone does not imply broad participation.

The movers panel has three views: Daily movers are strictly above +10% or below −10% versus the prior close; exactly +10% and −10% are excluded. The other views show 20-trading-session highs/lows and 52-week highs/lows (252 sessions). A preview shows up to five tickers and the true qualifying count; Full list keeps the selected date and data version. Ticker and available industry names link to their detail views.

Daily participation values are percentages of comparable stocks meeting each move threshold; counts are available in the tooltip or contributor drawer. The comparison matrix and sector/industry heatmaps mix measures with different units: returns and participation are percentages, RS is a percentile/rank measure, and counts are securities. Read the metric label and unit before comparing colors. In the RS-versus-velocity map, velocity is the change in RS percentile points; missing velocity is displayed at the neutral position, not treated as a measured zero change.

Breadth percentages use the comparable traded securities for that metric and session. Prices that are missing, invalid, quarantined, unchanged where a move is required, or too short for a lookback can be excluded. Use the numerator, denominator, and coverage status in the interface to understand what a percentage describes. The data-quality page explains missing or excluded inputs.

sections.heading: A practical review
steps: Start with the selected date, universe, benchmark, and RS model shown in the context controls.
Compare benchmark direction with advancing, declining, and moving-average participation.
Open a breadth reading to inspect contributors, comparable names, and exclusions for that date.
Use replay to compare another completed session; verify that its historical context is prepared before drawing a comparison.

sections.heading: Example research sequence
paragraphs: For a swing-research review, first note broad participation and the benchmark context; then compare the 1M/3M/6M leaders with the model-driven improving-leader lists. Screen candidates for a defined trend, high/low distance, and volume pattern, and check whether their industry or theme shows comparable strength. Carry names to a manual watchlist or save a dynamic screen, then record a dated journal thesis and the conditions that would invalidate it. Later, replay that session or run an event/cohort study to inspect how the observations developed. This is a repeatable research sequence, not a buy/sell signal or performance promise.

sections.heading: Health and interpretation
paragraphs: Health graphics show each raw reading in its original units: percentages for participation and volume share, percentage points for the new-high minus new-low spread. The active model's weights and normalized 0–100 component score appear only when available. Component details retain input counts and coverage. Missing readings or scores stay unavailable; the interface does not fill a partial composite or invent history. An observed/descriptive reading is not a probability or forecast, and a strict coverage gate can withhold scores when configured support is insufficient.

topics.title: Market Monitor
topics.summary: Compare fixed breadth thresholds across sessions and inspect exact contributors.

sections.heading: Fixed presets and custom comparison
paragraphs: The standard timeline uses fixed upside and downside move presets. A bar shows the share of comparable securities whose close-to-close move met that threshold over the selected window. Its denominator is the count with a valid comparable return, not the entire listed market. Optional counts show the underlying numerator and denominator; moving averages and deltas summarize the displayed metric over prior sessions.

Custom comparison controls are separate from the standard presets. Choose a rolling window in trading sessions and a percentage move, then apply it to see a separate timeline and export. A custom setting does not change the fixed preset definitions. Bar scales can be automatic for each comparison or shared for visual comparison.

sections.heading: Read and investigate a bar
steps: Choose the visible session range and whether to show counts, historical extremes, or averages and changes. Focus range scales bars within each metric group; full scale uses 0–100%.

Select a fixed metric title to open paired upside and downside history. Choose 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, or 5Y and focus or full-scale charting. The chart reads saved session measurements only; if dates are missing, prepare that context and check readiness before relying on the history.
Read a bar's historical percentile against its prior 252 comparable sessions; at least 60 prior readings are required. A percentile is unavailable when calibration is insufficient.
Use the session date to replay the market context for that day.
Select an upside or downside bar, or a session in the paired chart, to inspect that date's exact qualifying contributors, numerator, denominator, and exclusions.
Export the standard or custom timeline when you need a local analysis copy.

sections.heading: Historical extremes
paragraphs: Extreme markers compare each reading with its prepared prior-252-session distribution for the same metric; at least 60 comparable prior readings are required. The default highlights the top and bottom 5% (at or above the 95th percentile or at or below the 5th). You can choose rarer 2% extremes (98th/2nd) or the optional 10% setting (90th/10th). This changes highlighting only, not the saved reading or calibration. If history or coverage is insufficient, calibration is unavailable rather than estimated.

topics.title: Screener
topics.summary: Build repeatable filters from security metrics, ranks, and supported expressions.

sections.heading: Build a screen
steps: Choose a universe and analysis context before selecting fields; changing either can change the comparable population.
Add numeric, category, date, or boolean conditions. Combine conditions with nested AND/OR groups, then choose sort precedence, visible columns, computed columns, and pagination.
Use the high/low editor for distance from a rolling extreme or session age since a strict break. Save the definition when you want to reuse it.
Inspect the result count and field availability. A null value can mean insufficient history, unavailable source data, a quarantined interval, or an unprepared context.

sections.heading: Rolling high and low fields
paragraphs: Distance is the close relative to the highest high or lowest low in the selected rolling window. Strict age counts trading sessions since price strictly exceeded the prior rolling high or fell below the prior rolling low; equal highs and lows do not reset that clock. Age of the current extreme is a separate value. An event on the current session has age zero. A gap or unverified split crossing can make the field unavailable.

Windows are measured in trading sessions: 52 weeks is 252 sessions. Example filters include at least 30 sessions since a 20-session high or at least 250 since a 252-session low; these are filter values, not minimum-history requirements. The rolling window and prior-extreme event must be supported by contiguous, source-safe history. A saved screen can follow the latest completed prepared EOD or pin a historical date and data revision.

sections.heading: Expressions and limits
paragraphs: Computed columns and screen expressions support a validated set of numeric operations, comparisons, boolean logic, and functions such as rank, percentile, previous, change, min, max, abs, log, and coalesce. This is a safe metric-expression language, not arbitrary SQL or Python. Screen expressions do not make every ranking-model method available as a model formula.

Built-in Stockbee-style presets are fixed: 4% in one session, 25% in 63 sessions, 25% or 50% in 20 sessions, and 13% in 34 sessions. Custom rolling thresholds are separate; the app does not claim a proprietary Stockbee formula.

topics.title: Relative-strength rankings
topics.summary: Compare returns and model ranks within the selected comparable population.

sections.heading: Return leader lists
paragraphs: Independent split-adjusted return lists are available for 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year. Each period has its own eligible/comparable population. The adjustable top-percent cutoff defaults to 2%; the list size is the ceiling of population times cutoff. A smaller population can therefore produce fewer results. Rows link to the corresponding TradingView chart, and selected rows can be carried to a watchlist.

These period lists answer which securities led a particular interval. Model-driven lists answer different questions, including Top RS, Fast Improvers, New Top-Decile Entries, Emerging Leaders, Industry Leaders, and Weakening Leaders. A model list is not interchangeable with a raw return list.

definitions.text: The built-in composite model combines split-adjusted 12-, 6-, 3-, and 1-month returns using weights of 40%, 30%, 20%, and 10%, then ranks securities within the selected comparable universe.
definitions.formula: score = 0.40 × return(252 sessions) + 0.30 × return(126) + 0.20 × return(63) + 0.10 × return(21)

definitions.text: Percentiles are relative to eligible comparable securities in the current universe and context. Higher percentiles indicate stronger relative rank; insufficient lookback history remains null rather than being filled with zero.

sections.heading: Create a model and choose a date
steps: Select a built-in model or create a versioned model with supported return windows and one of the available scoring methods.
Use latest mode for the most recent completed, prepared EOD; use replay for a historical date and pinned data revision.
Check the comparable population and history sufficiency before comparing ranks across dates.
paragraphs: Rank ties use deterministic ordering, but equal scores do not imply different economic strength. Model results depend on the chosen universe, benchmark, price basis, calculation version, and available history.

topics.title: Industries and themes
topics.summary: Compare group participation, leadership, relative performance, and changes over time.

sections.heading: How group views work
paragraphs: Group views aggregate security metrics for the selected classification system and context. Depending on the panel, you can compare group breadth, median or cap-weighted performance, relative strength, leadership, rank changes, persistence, turnover, and parent-relative results. Drill into a group to inspect its securities and compare the exact date's inputs.

Themes are user-defined collections and can overlap industries. A theme's summary describes its members; it does not create an independent provider classification. Group changes can reflect both security performance and changes in eligible membership.

sections.heading: Choose a classification carefully
paragraphs: Nasdaq typed-reference classifications represent a captured current reference, not a full historical classification series. For dated historical industry analysis, SEC/SIC is the available alternative, with the caveat that SEC identity mapping is through the current catalog and does not establish a complete point-in-time universe. If a group lacks prior classifications, historical comparison can be unavailable or incomplete.

Rotation and leadership persistence charts compare prepared sessions and show cohort or comparable counts where applicable. Nulls mean the source cohort or required history is not available; they should not be read as zero leadership.

sections.heading: A useful workflow
steps: Choose the date, universe, classification, and model, then compare groups on both absolute and parent-relative measures.
Open a group to review contributors and breadth denominators before concluding that the whole group is participating.
Use a saved theme to compare a consistent custom basket across prepared sessions.

topics.title: Historical explorer and studies
topics.summary: Replay prepared market history and evaluate cohorts or events with explicit availability limits.

sections.heading: Historical series and replay
paragraphs: Historical Explorer plots selected metrics for a chosen universe, model, benchmark, classification, and data revision. Daily and weekly series may include breadth, ranks, group leadership, and transition or persistence measures. Selecting a date changes the analytical context; use the displayed date and revision to confirm what is being compared.

Historical observations are constrained by the source records available for that date. The current warehouse has a broader captured history beginning in late 2016, while the earliest portion contains only a small sample. A complete sequence of dates is not proof that every US security was present on every date. Historical float, complete ticker-reuse continuity, and terminal returns for delisted securities are not established.

sections.heading: Cohorts, events, and analogs
paragraphs: Event studies measure forward returns after a defined market event; cohorts compare a selected set of securities. Transition analysis counts comparable changes between prepared periods, and analogs compare current context with earlier observations. Results should show sample size, comparison counts, and censoring. Right-censored outcomes have not yet completed their forward window.

The system uses availability-aware dates to avoid treating a later-published input as known earlier. That safeguard cannot compensate for missing historical classifications, prices, or delisted terminal data. These are descriptive studies, not estimates of future performance.

sections.heading: Prepare before reading
steps: Select the exact date and context, then check Data Quality or job status if the chart reports unprepared or partial history.
Queue the specific history job when needed and wait for completion; normal read requests do not silently compute a cold full-catalog history grid.
Export plotted data when you need to review or reproduce a result outside the app.

topics.title: Market Journal
topics.summary: Save dated research notes and structured market reports with versioned prompts and factors.

sections.heading: Reports and prompts
paragraphs: Market Journal stores daily report revisions, a versioned Markdown prompt, and structured numeric factors. Generated reports include sentiment, market health, risk posture, and confidence fields, plus any configured factors. The report records its availability time and next eligible session so a historical study does not pretend the text was available before publication.

Retrospective reports are labeled and excluded from backtests by default. A Claude API key is optional and must be configured in Journal Settings before real generation; no report should be described as Claude-generated unless the provider response was actually received. The key is encrypted locally.

sections.heading: Keep notes separate
paragraphs: Personal notes are stored separately from generated reports and remain local. A note is not sent to Anthropic unless you explicitly opt in for that generation. Avoid putting secrets or account credentials in a prompt or note. The active prompt and custom factor definitions are versioned so later edits do not silently rewrite prior report context.

sections.heading: Use it in research
steps: Review the selected market context and data quality before generating a report.
Edit and publish a prompt revision, then define numeric factors with clear labels and descriptions.
Save your own note separately; opt in only if you want that note included in the request.
Use factor charts and backtests to inspect recorded values, respecting each report's availability time and the default exclusion of retrospective entries.

topics.title: Watchlists
topics.summary: Track manually selected securities or the current members of a saved screen.

sections.heading: Manual and dynamic lists
paragraphs: A manual watchlist stores securities you explicitly add. You can add a ticker from search, a screener result, a rankings list, or a contributor drawer, then remove names without changing the source screen. A dynamic watchlist is linked to a saved screen and evaluates that screen's membership rather than maintaining an independent manual member set.

Dynamic membership can change as the latest completed EOD context changes. If the source screen is pinned to a historical date or data revision, the watchlist is a replay of that pinned definition. The page labels live versus pinned behavior when the context is available.

sections.heading: Create a watchlist
steps: Choose Create Watchlist and select Manual selections or Dynamic from a saved screen.
For a manual list, add securities by ticker or carry selected rows from another market view.
For a dynamic list, save the source screen first and confirm whether it follows latest EOD or a pinned replay.
Open a row for stock detail or its TradingView chart; use the screen's own filters to change dynamic membership.

sections.heading: Interpret membership
paragraphs: A watchlist is an organizational tool, not an endorsement or trade instruction. Missing or unranked securities can remain in a manual list even when they are excluded from a particular ranking denominator.

topics.title: Saved screens
topics.summary: Store filter, column, sort, and context choices for repeatable latest or historical research.

sections.heading: Save a reusable definition
paragraphs: A saved screen stores its filters, supported expressions, columns, sort order, and analysis context. Latest-mode screens follow the latest completed prepared EOD publication. Historical screens can pin a date and data version so their definition can be replayed against that context. A model or source revision may also be pinned where the saved definition specifies it.

When a definition depends on rolling high/low measures, save or prepare the required windows. Preparation status is tied to the exact context; a completed archive for another model, benchmark, universe, classification, or warehouse version does not guarantee this screen is ready.

sections.heading: Use and revise screens
steps: Build and inspect the screen in the Screener, then choose Save Screen.
Choose whether to follow latest data or pin the selected historical session.
Open a saved screen to evaluate its current or pinned membership; inspect null fields and comparable counts.
Create a new saved version when the research rule changes so prior definitions remain identifiable.

sections.heading: What a match means
paragraphs: A match means the available metrics satisfied the saved predicate in the chosen context. It does not certify complete market membership or source coverage. Expressions support the app's safe numeric/filter language, not arbitrary database queries or every possible RS scoring formula.

topics.title: Alerts
topics.summary: Evaluate saved rules for market breadth, stock conditions, screens, groups, or regimes.

sections.heading: Supported rules
paragraphs: Alert rules can watch a breadth threshold, a stock condition entering or leaving a condition, saved-screen membership, industry-rank entry, or a market-health regime change. Rules have a name and active state. When an evaluation matches, the app stores a dated event with the evaluated context so you can review what triggered it.

Alerts are evaluated against completed analytical sessions and available prepared inputs. A missing source value or incomplete context can prevent a condition from matching; it should not be interpreted as a negative event. The event log is a research record, not an execution or broker integration.

sections.heading: Create and evaluate
steps: Open Alerts and choose Create Rule.
Select the trigger type and specify its threshold, screen, group, or regime condition.
Save the rule and confirm it is enabled. Pause or edit the rule when its research definition changes.
Evaluate a completed session when available, then inspect the event's date, universe, and source context.

sections.heading: Avoid overreading alerts
paragraphs: A triggered rule reports that a defined condition occurred in the data. It does not recommend a trade or predict a return. Review the underlying prices, denominators, and data-quality notes before using an event in a study.

topics.title: Settings and data quality
topics.summary: Choose analytical context, inspect source coverage, manage local imports, and configure Journal access.

sections.heading: Context and readiness
paragraphs: The active context can include date, universe, RS model, benchmark, classification, price basis, coverage threshold, and warehouse revision. The same metric can differ when one of these changes. Data Quality and job status expose received records, exclusions, source errors, and whether a specific calculation context has been prepared.

Recent provider imports do not automatically mean recent analytics are ready. The warehouse import, raw capture receipt, strict universe coverage, and prepared analytics are separate states. For broad datasets, preparation runs as queued background work and can take hours or be held by a disk-space admission guard. Check the exact requested context before interpreting a chart.

sections.heading: Provider and security settings
paragraphs: Provider credentials are read server-side from private local settings. Do not paste keys into help, browser code, or saved research. EODHD daily prices, bulk history, split actions, and delisted listings are available under the configured account; fundamentals and ticker-rename requests have returned 403. Historical public float and complete point-in-time membership remain unavailable in current sources.

Journal Settings can store an Anthropic API key encrypted locally. A key is optional; without it, live Claude generation is not available. Prompt and factor revisions can still be edited without representing them as generated reports.

sections.heading: Operator workflow
steps: Check warehouse status, data quality, and queued jobs before changing provider or calculation settings.
Use targeted imports or repairs for known gaps; avoid forcing a full history restart unless that is intended.
After an import, check current, recent, and history preparation status separately.
Create and verify a backup before a large import or destructive recovery operation.

topics.title: Ticker detail
topics.summary: Review a security's price history, relative strength, volume, range metrics, and provenance.

sections.heading: What is on the ticker page
paragraphs: Ticker detail is organized into Last session, Price & trend, Volume & participation, Liquidity & fundamentals, and All metrics. Changing sections filters the already loaded view and does not request a new calculation. Period tables align moving-average and volume measures by session window so comparisons stay on the same row.

The price chart shows split-adjusted OHLCV history and can export the plotted data as CSV. Use the TradingView link to open the matching security chart in a separate research tool. Float turnover requires dated public-float observations; when float or another source field is unavailable, the value remains blank rather than being estimated.

Metrics are scoped to the selected date, model, benchmark, price basis, universe, and data/calculation revision. The ticker's loaded-history high is limited to the history actually present for that security; it is not necessarily its all-time high. Corporate actions and unresolved source-quality intervals can change which measures are usable.

definitions.text: The close's relative distance from the highest high in the selected session window. Values near zero are close to that window's high; negative values are below it.
Trading sessions since a session strictly exceeded the prior rolling high or fell below the prior rolling low. Ties do not reset the counter; the current extreme's age is shown separately.
252 trading sessions. A window can be unavailable until its required comparable history is prepared and source-safe.

sections.heading: Investigate the record
steps: Confirm symbol identity, selected context, listing dates, and loaded history span.
Compare the candle chart with action/provenance notes when the return or volume series looks discontinuous.
Use watchlist or export actions to carry the security into a saved workflow; review exclusions before treating a missing field as zero.

topics.title: Coverage and source limitations
topics.summary: Separate provider capture, warehouse import, universe coverage, and prepared analytics.

definitions.text: Provider responses and manifests saved for audit or re-import. Capture receipt counts describe requests and records received, not market-wide analytical coverage.
Validated, identity-mapped observations committed into a specific data version. Invalid rows, stale symbols, pre-listing bars, ambiguous aliases, and quarantined windows can be withheld.
The fraction of eligible securities or observations represented for a selected date and metric. The denominator depends on universe rules and valid source history.
Calculated snapshots and archives available for the exact model, date, benchmark, classification, and data/calculation version requested.

sections.heading: Known limits
paragraphs: EODHD price, bulk-history, action, and delisted-listing endpoints are available under the configured account. Fundamentals and rename endpoints have returned 403. SEC/SIC and Nasdaq current-reference sources add useful classifications, but do not provide complete historical membership. Historical public float is not established, delisted records do not have complete terminal returns, and ticker reuse needs more source evidence.

Some early historical dates contain only a small sample, while wider market coverage begins later. Recent captures can be partial, and a partial receipt does not trigger an automatic full-history redownload on every scheduled refresh. Raw source, corrections, received counts, and analytics readiness should be checked independently.

sections.heading: Coverage-aware interpretation
paragraphs: Observed/descriptive metrics report what the current comparable set shows. Strict health applies configured minimum support and can withhold a score. Neither mode repairs missing source history. A percentage must be read with its numerator, denominator, and date; changing the universe changes the question being answered.

topics.title: ChartBook
topics.summary: Combine saved lists into a deduplicated chart review with dated notes and bookmarks.

sections.heading: Build and review a book
steps: Create a book, then select built-in lists, saved screens, manual watchlists, or manual tickers/security IDs. ChartBook deduplicates by permanent security ID and shows a badge for every source that includes each stock.
Review the selected session, data revision, source badges, and source status. Choose a default manual watchlist if you want B or Bookmark to save the current stock there.
Move between stocks with Next/Previous or the keyboard. Save a note for the current stock and date; notes and watchlist bookmarks persist.

sections.heading: Chart ranges and overlays

definitions.text: Six months (126 trading sessions). Available ranges are 1M/21 sessions, 3M/63, 6M/126, 1Y/252, and 5Y/1,260. The chart reports actual priced sessions and date bounds; a 5Y selection can display less than five years when saved price history is shorter.
A marker shows an individual stock's close-to-close move when its absolute daily return is at least 4%. It is not a market breadth percentage.

Comparison curves are rebased to the stock close at a shared or first usable anchor so they can be shown on the stock-price scale. They are not raw benchmark or industry prices. Missing or quarantined sessions remain gaps.

paragraphs: Toggle 20-session and 50-session moving averages, SPY, Industry, and the ±4% move strip. Point inspection shows the session date, available OHLCV, stock close/return, and rebased comparison values. The status below the chart identifies the comparison method and unavailable inputs.

Dated industry membership is used when available. A current-member equal-weight industry proxy can be prepared for the latest reconstructed session and applied retrospectively; it does not represent historical constituents. Historical industry curves can be unavailable when dated group membership is missing.

sections.heading: Keyboard and safe typing

definitions.text: Space: next stock; Shift+Space or Left Arrow: previous; B: bookmark; V: longer range; M: 3M; N: note; Escape: dismiss the chart point display. Focus the chart and use Up/Down to inspect sessions or Home/End to jump to the first/last plotted point.

paragraphs: Review shortcuts are disabled while a dialog is open or focus is in an input, text area, select, or editable text. Typing a note therefore does not navigate or bookmark stocks.

topics.title: Stock Lists
topics.summary: Browse period-return leaders and model-driven stock lists separately from saved screen rules.

sections.heading: Choose the list you need
paragraphs: Period-return lists rank their own comparable population for the selected period and allow an adjustable top-percent cutoff. Model lists such as Top RS, Fast Improvers, and Emerging Leaders use the selected RS model and answer a different ranking question. Counts and ranks depend on the chosen date, universe, model, and available history.

Stock Lists can open a saved screen, but the screen definition remains in Saved Screens, the canonical place to build and revise reusable filters, sorting, and columns. Configure RS models in Settings. A Stock List is not itself a custom model formula.

sections.heading: A repeatable workflow
steps: Choose a period-return list or an RS model list and inspect its comparable population.
Adjust the top-percent cutoff for a return list when needed; use filters and columns to inspect candidates.
Save durable filter rules under Saved Screens, configure ranking models in Settings, and carry selected stocks into a watchlist or ChartBook for review.

topics.title: Definitions and calculations
topics.summary: Shared terms used across market breadth, relative strength, history, and health.

definitions.text: Securities eligible for a specific metric in a selected universe, date, and context after required price/history checks.
Qualifying securities divided by comparable securities for that metric and session.
A security's position relative to comparable securities. Higher percentile means stronger relative rank; it is not a future-return probability.

Change in relative-strength percentile over the selected number of weeks, measured in percentile points. Missing velocity means the comparison is unavailable; a neutral map position is a display fallback, not an observed zero change.
End-of-day data for a completed market session. Latest-mode screens and reports follow completed and prepared publications, not an unfinished intraday quote.
A descriptive score based on available component observations and shown with support/coverage information.
A score made available only when configured component coverage and sample minimums are satisfied; otherwise the score is withheld.
The app's observed NYSE common-stock ratio-adjusted summation series. It is not the published NYSE all-issues NYSI.
definitions.formula: net advances = 1000 × (advancers − decliners) / (advancers + decliners); oscillator = fast EMA − slow EMA; summation = cumulative oscillator after warmup

sections.heading: More metric notes
paragraphs: Split-adjusted returns account for verified splits in the price series. Total-return mode additionally depends on supported dividend inputs; missing provider fundamentals or corporate events should not be invented. Rank is an ordinal position within the comparable universe, while percentile provides a normalized relative position.

An SMA is the simple mean of values over a stated number of sessions. An EMA weights recent observations more heavily: EMA(t) = α × value(t) + (1 − α) × EMA(t−1). The summation proxy starts its fast/slow EMAs and cumulative value at zero, derives a fast-minus-slow exponential oscillator, and publishes after its valid-coverage warmup; gaps restart that warmup.
